_readme: Machine-readable expected-file sets for the FROZEN question set in
cardwise-eval-questions.md. The frozen file is not edited; this resolves
its prose cells ('wherever persistence lives') into concrete paths so
recall can be computed. Where this disagrees with or extends the frozen
cell, 'note' says so and 'confidence' flags how sure the resolution is.
Resolved against CardWise @ 2026-09-09 by reading the code.

questions.q: Where is the logic that picks the best card for a purchase?
Where is the app's global UI state held on Android?
Where are the core domain models defined on iOS?
Where is the seed/demo data defined?
Which file defines the shared/reusable UI components on Android?
Where is the Supabase project configured?
Where is the form for adding or editing a card in the admin panel?
Where is the database schema for a user's saved cards first defined?
questions.note: Resolves 'earliest relevant migration'. init.sql creates user_cards (user_id, template_id, nickname, is_discover_category_activated, active_discover_category, created_at).

questions.q: Where is the app's navigation/entry point on Android?
Where is the wallet screen implemented on iOS?
How does the recommendation engine rank cards - what inputs does it score on?
What settings can a user change, and where are they persisted?
questions.note: Resolves 'wherever persistence lives' to CatalogStore.kt, which owns the only SharedPreferences ('cardwise_catalog'). AppState.kt holds the in-memory settings state and is a defensible third file.

questions.q: What does the home screen show, and where does that data come from?
How is a reward category represented in the database schema?
questions.note: Resolves 'relevant migration' to init.sql. 20260714120000_housing_category.sql and 20260718100000_channel_rewards.sql extend categories later.

questions.q: What happens when a user adds a card to their wallet?
What does the earliest migration create, and what does the most recent one add?
How does the admin panel talk to Supabase, and what does it send?
questions.note: Resolves 'or a sibling in admin/' to supabaseClient.js, which owns the client.

questions.q: What does the CI pipeline run on a pull request?
questions.note: Narrows the frozen '.github/workflows/*.yml'. Only ci.yml has a pull_request trigger; ios.yml is workflow_dispatch and release.yml is tag-only. Scoring against all three would be wrong.

questions.q: What edge cases does the Android recommendation test suite cover?
How is the iOS project split between CardWise and CardWiseKit?
questions.note: Resolves 'iOS package manifest' to Package.swift. Three files in a 5-chunk budget.

questions.q: What calls the recommendation engine on Android?
questions.note: EXTENDS the frozen cell. It says 'callers in ui/', which catches AppState.kt:221 (repository.recommend) but omits CardWiseRepository.kt:31, which actually instantiates RecommendationEngine. Nothing else in ui/ references it.

questions.q: Which screens read from AppState?
questions.note: 4 files inside a 5-chunk budget: near-zero headroom by construction.

questions.q: Which tables does the Android app read from?
questions.note: Resolves 'migrations + Android data layer'. init.sql defines official_card_templates, merchant_mappings, card_requests, user_cards.

questions.q: What writes to the cards table?
questions.note: Resolves 'relevant migration' to init.sql, which creates official_card_templates.

questions.q: Where is CardWiseComponents used?
questions.note: 5 files in a 5-chunk budget: only passes on a perfect top-5. Verified by grep; these are exactly the importers.

questions.q: Do the Kotlin and Swift recommendation engines produce the same result for the same input?
How does the settings screen differ between iOS and Android?
How does the wallet screen differ between iOS and Android?
Which fields of the cards table are used by all three clients?
questions.note: Resolves 'Android data layer' to SupabaseDtos.kt (the DTO mapping). 4 files across 3 platforms in a 5-chunk budget.

questions.q: Is the same validation applied on Android, iOS, and the admin panel?
questions.note: Resolves 'the three validation sites, wherever they are'. LOW confidence: there is no single obvious validation site per platform; DTO decoding is the closest analogue on Android/iOS. This resolution should be reviewed before the number is reported.
